column1: Why is a test that passes 19 times in 20 worse than one that always fails?
column2: It is non-deterministic: a failure can't be reproduced, so it teaches people to re-run and ignore red. A consistently failing test points at a cause.
A test that pins down what code currently does (not what it should do), written before changing code you don't fully understand. (Feathers)

column1: Two reasons a file listed in .gitignore can still be tracked
column2: 1. The file was committed before the ignore rule (ignore never affects tracked files; use git rm --cached). 2. The pattern doesn't match, e.g. written as UTF-16 so git sees NUL bytes.

Why use Math.imul(a, b) instead of a * b for 32-bit hashing/PRNGs?
column2: a * b is a float64 multiply: products above 2^53 lose low bits. Math.imul gives the exact low 32 bits of the integer product, like C.

r % n over a range whose size isn't a multiple of n makes small results more likely. E.g. r in 0..7 (8 values), n = 3: 0 and 1 occur 3 times each, 2 only twice. Fix: reject the uneven tail and redraw.
For independent uniforms u1 in (0,1], u2 in [0,1): z = sqrt(-2 ln u1) · cos(2π u2) is standard normal. u1 must not be 0 (ln 0 = -∞).

column1: Ring buffer: what is the write index after pushing 6 samples into capacity 4 (starting at 0)?
column2: 6 mod 4 = 2. The buffer holds [5,6,3,4] in storage order; the oldest-first view is [3,4,5,6].

column1: Why does pitch.ts zero-pad to ≥ 2N before the FFT autocorrelation?
column2: The FFT computes circular correlation; without padding, lags wrap around and alias. Padding to ≥ 2N makes circular equal linear for all lags < N.
n(τ) = 2·r(τ) / m(τ), where r is the autocorrelation and m(τ) = Σ (x_j² + x_{j+τ}²) over the overlap. It lies in [-1, 1], with 1 = perfectly periodic at lag τ.

column1: Why does MPM pick the first key maximum ≥ k·highest (k = 0.9 in OnStand), not the highest?
column2: Peaks at 2× and 3× the period can be as high as (or higher than) the true one. The highest would read an octave or more low. The first strong one is the fundamental period.

column1: What does a DC offset do to the NSDF, and what is the minimal fix?
column2: It adds roughly c² to every lag, pushing the NSDF towards +1: it never crosses zero, so no key maxima are found → null. Fix: subtract the window mean before the energy sums and the FFT.

column1: The "red commit" in test-first bug fixing
column2: A commit containing only the new failing test. It proves the test can fail, i.e. that it actually detects the bug, before the fix lands.
